arxiv-2109-06306.title: BERT for Target Apps Selection: Analyzing the Diversity and Performance of BERT in Unified Mobile Search Conference: CIKM; 2021; Australia
arxiv-2109-06306.creator: Negin Ghasemi, Mohammad Aliannejadi, Djoerd Hiemstra
arxiv-2109-06306.description: Abstract . A unified mobile search framework aims to identify the mobile apps that can satisfy a user’s information need and route the user’s query to them. Previous work has shown that resource descriptions for mobile apps are sparse as they rely on the app’s previous queries.

arxiv-2111-09744.title: Covered Information Disentanglement: Model Transparency via Unbiased Permutation Importance
arxiv-2111-09744.creator: João Pereira, Erik S.G. Stroes, Aeilko H. Zwinderman, Evgeni Levin
arxiv-2111-09744.description: Abstract Model transparency is a prerequisite in many domains and an increasingly popular area in machine learning research. In the medical domain, for instance, unveiling the mechanisms behind a disease often has higher priority than the diagnostic itself since it might dictate or guide potential treatments and research directions.

arxiv-2202-01567.description: Abstract A garden G G is populated by n ≥ 1 n\geq 1 bamboos b 1 , b 2 , … , b n b_{1},b_{2},...,b_{n} with the respective daily growth rates h 1 ≥ h 2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ h n h_{1}\geq h_{2}\geq\dots\geq h_{n} . It is assumed that the initial heights of bamboos are zero.

arxiv-2204-11164.title: Are Your Reviewers Being Treated Equally? Discovering Subgroup Structures to Improve Fairness in Spam Detection Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2204-11164.creator: Jiaxin Liu, Yuefei Lyu, Xi Zhang, Sihong Xie
arxiv-2204-11164.description: Abstract . User-generated reviews of products are vital assets of online commerce, such as Amazon and Yelp, while fake reviews are prevalent to mislead customers. GNN is the state-of-the-art method that detects suspicious reviewers by exploiting the topologies of the graph connecting reviewers, reviews, and target products.

arxiv-2301-04979.title: Role of mush complex viscosity in modulating axial topography in mid-oceanic ridges
arxiv-2301-04979.creator: Joyjeet Sen, Shamik Sarkar, Nibir Mandal
arxiv-2301-04979.description: Abstract This article exploits the interaction dynamics of the elastic oceanic crust with the underlying mush complexes (MC) to constrain the axial topography of mid-ocean ridges (MORs). The effective viscosity ( μ e ​ f ​ f \mu_{eff} ) of MC beneath MORs is recognized as the crucial factor in modulating their axial high versus flat topography.

arxiv-2311-18032.title: Gravitational wave signals from long lasting binary–single black hole encounters. Journal: .
arxiv-2311-18032.creator: Elena Codazzo, Matteo Di Giovanni, Jan Harms
arxiv-2311-18032.description: Abstract In the dense regions of star clusters, close encounters with black holes (BHs) can occur giving rise to a new class of gravitational-wave (GW) signals. Binary-single encounters between three BHs are expected to dominate the rate of signals from unbound systems in the frequency band of terrestrial GW detectors.

arxiv-2409-20170.title: Superabelian logics
arxiv-2409-20170.creator: Petr Cintula, Filip Jankovec, Carles Noguera
arxiv-2409-20170.description: Abstract This paper presents a unified algebraic study of a family of logics related to Abelian logic ( Ab {\mathrm{Ab}} ), the logic of Abelian lattice-ordered groups. We treat Ab {\mathrm{Ab}} as the base system and refer to its expansions as superabelian logics . The paper focuses on two main families of expansions.

arxiv-2507-11326.title: Euclid preparation
arxiv-2507-11326.creator: Euclid Collaboration: B. Kubik, R. Barbier, J. Clemens, S. Ferriol, A. Secroun, G. Smadja, W. Gillard, N. Fourmanoit, A. Ealet, S. Conseil, J. Zoubian, R. Kohley, J.-C. arxiv-2507-11326.description: Abstract The paper describes the objectives, design and findings of the pre-launch ground characterisation campaigns of the Euclid infrared detectors. The aim of the ground characterisations is to evaluate the performance of the detectors, to calibrate the pixel response, and to derive the pixel response correction methods.

arxiv-2510-27248.title: The Role of Search Engines in the Amplification and Suppression of LGBTIQ+ Polarization
arxiv-2510-27248.creator: Ronja Rönnback, Chris Emmery, Marie Šafář Postma, Filip Milde, Jan Charvát, Henry Brighton
arxiv-2510-27248.description: Abstract Search engines are used and trusted by hundreds of millions of people every day. However, the algorithms used by search engines to index, filter, and rank web content are inherently biased, and will necessarily prefer some views and opinions at the expense of others. In this article, we examine how these algorithmic biases amplify and suppress polarizing content.

pmc-10518816.title: Metastable Amorphous Dispersions of Hydrophobic Naphthalene Compounds Can Be Formed in Water without Stabilizing Agents via the “Ouzo Effect”
pmc-10518816.creator: Julie M Belanger, Joseph A Cirilo
pmc-10518816.description: Hydrophobic molecules dissolved in water-miscible organic solvents are used in vitro for biological membrane studies and for testing of potential pharmaceuticals in high-throughput screenings. When these solutions are introduced into an aqueous environment, it is possible that metastable “ouzo-like” dispersions form from liquid–liquid phase separation.

pmc-10733149.title: Biological carbon pump estimate based on multidecadal hydrographic data
pmc-10733149.creator: Wei-Lei Wang, Weiwei Fu, Frédéric A. C. Le Moigne, Robert T. Letscher, Yi Liu, Jin-Ming Tang, François W. Primeau
pmc-10733149.description: The transfer of photosynthetically produced organic carbon from surface to mesopelagic waters draws carbon dioxide from the atmosphere1. However, current observation-based estimates disagree on the strength of this biological carbon pump (BCP)2. Earth system models (ESMs) also exhibit a large spread of BCP estimates, indicating limited representations of the known carbon export pathways3.

pmc-11509309.title: Potential of Marine Sponge Metabolites against Prions: Bromotyrosine Derivatives, a Family of Interest
pmc-11509309.creator: Maha Sinane, Colin Grunberger, Lucile Gentile, Céline Moriou, Victorien Chaker, Pierre Coutrot, Alain Guenneguez, Marie-Aude Poullaouec, Solène Connan, Valérie Stiger-Pouvreau, Mayalen Zubia, Yannick Fleury, Stéphane Cérantola, Nelly Kervarec, Ali Al-Mourabit, Sylvain Petek, Cécile Voisset, Concetta
pmc-11509309.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The screening of 166 extracts from tropical marine organisms (invertebrates, macroalgae) and 3 cyclolipopeptides from microorganisms against yeast prions highlighted the potential of Verongiida sponges to prevent the propagation of prions. We isolated the known compounds purealidin Q (1), aplysamine-2 (2), pseudoceratinine A (3), aerophobin-2 (4), aplysamine-1 (5), and pseudoceratinine B (6) for the first time from the Wallisian sponge Suberea laboutei.

pmc-11655352.creator: Francis Nimmo, Thorsten Kleine, Alessandro Morbidelli
pmc-11655352.description: The last giant impact on Earth is thought to have formed the Moon1. The timing of this event can be determined by dating the different rocks assumed to have crystallized from the lunar magma ocean (LMO). This has led to a wide range of estimates for the age of the Moon between 4.35 and 4.

pmc-11860835.title: What link between violence against women and self-esteem?
pmc-11860835.creator: M Abdelkefi, R Feki, A Turki, I Gassara, N Smaoui, S Omri, N Charfi, L Zouari, J Ben Thabet, M Maalej Bouali, M Maalej
pmc-11860835.description: IntroductionViolence against women is a public health problem worldwide and a violation of human rights. It affects women’s lives due to its potential short-, medium- or long-term physical and psychological consequences.ObjectivesThe aim of our study is to explore the link between violence against women and self-esteem.

pmc-11980621.title: A one health study on phylogenetics and risk of pathogenic intestinal parasites at a ranch in Inner Mongolia
pmc-11980621.creator: Ziran Mo, Jingwei Quan, Bin Xu, Huixia Yu, Junyan Li, Xiaoping Luo, Qimuge Wuyun, Jian Li, Wenbin Yang, Wei Hu
pmc-11980621.description: Cryptosporidium, Giardia duodenalis, and Enterocytozoon bieneusi are widespread zoonotic pathogens causing gastrointestinal diseases in humans and various animal species. Inner Mongolia, a major beef production region in China, there is a notable absence of comprehensive research on intestinal parasitism. Thus, timely and comprehensive diagnosis is essential to mitigate disease spread and minimize economic losses in the livestock industry.

pmc-13114419.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Prognosis, Recurrence Prediction, and Treatment Outcomes in Laryngeal Cancer: A Systematic Review
pmc-13114419.creator: Hadi Afandi Al-Hakami, Ismail A. Abdullah, Nora S. Almutairi, Rimaz R. Aldawsari, Ghadah Ali Alluqmani, Halah Ahmed Fallatah, Yara Saud Alsulami, Elyas Mohammed Alasiri, Rahaf D. Alsufyani, Raghad Ayman Alorabi, Reffal Mohammad Aldainiy
pmc-13114419.description: Simple SummaryPredicting response to treatment and prognosis remains a challenging aspect in laryngeal cancer since traditional methods, such as the tumor staging system, do not always reflect the complexity of the disease. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have provided high potential in analyzing complex medical data and improving predictions in cancer care.

pmc-13166234.title: Analysis of public perception and socio-demographic drivers of genetically modified organisms in Iran
pmc-13166234.creator: Mohammad Ahmadabadi, Zahra Dehghanian, Rana Valizadeh Kamran, Maghsoud Pazhouhandeh, Ali Aryan
pmc-13166234.description: The rapid growth in the world’s population poses a significant threat to food security, making genetically modified organisms (GMOs) an important potential solution. Alongside technological advancements, public awareness of GMOs – including their benefits and existing challenges – plays a crucial role in their acceptance and use within communities.

pmc-13210032.title: Validity and reliability of the persian adapted version of the labor pain relief attitude questionnaire for pregnant women (P-LPRAQ-p)
pmc-13210032.creator: Maryam Safarnavadeh, Leili Salehi, Marjan Havaei
pmc-13210032.description: BACKGROUND:Labor pain, as one of the inevitable pains among women, is generally tolerable for most women. The present study aimed to assess the cultural adaption and psychometric adequacy of the Labor Pain Relief Attitude Questionnaire (LPRAQ) for pregnant women.MATERIALS AND METHOD:This psychometric study was conducted in four distinct phases.

pmc-13237017.title: Integrating transformer-based credibility signals into neural collaborative filtering for fake review-aware recommendation
pmc-13237017.creator: Yasmeen Abdelmohsen, Khaled Wassif, Nagy Ramadan
pmc-13237017.description: Online recommender systems (RS) face growing trust challenges as deceptive reviews distort user feedback. Although RS optimisation and fake review detection have advanced separately, integrating credibility signals directly into recommendation training remains underexplored. This study proposes the Fake-Review-Aware Recommender System (FRARS), which embeds transformer-based deception probabilities into the training objective of a Neural Matrix Factorisation (NeuMF) model.

pmc-13311667.title: Prospective policy analysis of healthcare workforce policies for effective non-communicable disease prevention and management in Meghalaya, India
pmc-13311667.creator: Ankur Nair, Pratheeba John, Rajeev Sadanandan
pmc-13311667.description: This study presents a prospective policy analysis of healthcare workforce (human resources for health, HRH) reforms in Meghalaya, India, a state facing dual challenges of a rising burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and persistent inequities in access to medical and public health specialists.
